extracted.intended_audience: health researchers, authors, peer reviewers, journal editors, guideline developers
extracted.subtask_description: A bibliographic/index page listing reporting guidelines and checklists for designing, conducting, and reporting health research across many study types; intended as a reference for authors, reviewers and editors to apply appropriate reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines (library/umbrella)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides a library/index of reporting guidelines (checklists and explanation documents) that specify recommended reporting items for many study types to enhance quality and transparency of health research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key reporting guidelines are displayed; entries include guideline names, extensions, and links to checklists and explanation/elaboration documents. Use the relevant guideline for the study design/type being reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT (Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines and checklist for reporting randomised trials (CONSORT statement and many CONSORT extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple CONSORT extensions are listed (e.g., for adaptive designs, harms, nonpharmacologic treatments, dose-finding, cluster trials, N-of-1 trials, trials using cohorts/routinely collected data, trials modified due to COVID-19). Authors and reviewers should apply the main CONSORT checklist and any extension relevant to trial design or intervention type.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist and guidance for reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses (including PRISMA 2020 and many PRISMA extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes extensions for living systematic reviews, scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR), network meta-analyses, DTA, equity-focused reviews, scoping and other topic-specific extensions. Apply the PRISMA checklist appropriate to the review type.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE (Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting recommendations for observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) including many STROBE extensions for specific subfields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions listed include STROBE-MR, STROBE-Vet, STROBE-nut, STROBE-EQUITY, and many topic-specific adaptations. Select the STROBE checklist and relevant extension for observational study reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist and guidance for reporting clinical trial protocols (SPIRIT) and extensions (e.g., SPIRIT-AI, SPIRIT-Path).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPIRIT to structure and report trial protocols; apply extensions for specific interventions such as AI, pathology, or other specialized areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD (Standards for Reporting Diagnostic accuracy studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies (STARD) and related extensions (e.g., STARD-BLCM, STARDdem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow STARD items when reporting diagnostic/prognostic accuracy studies; use extensions where modelling or specific methods are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD (Transparent Reporting of multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guideline for reporting studies that develop or validate multivariable prediction models (and TRIPOD-related extensions, e.g., TRIPOD-Cluster, TRIPOD-LLM, TRIPOD+AI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should report on model development, validation, performance metrics, and intended use; apply AI/cluster-specific extensions when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE (CAse REport)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consensus-based clinical case reporting guideline (CARE) and extensions (e.g., CARE-DN, CARE-radiology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CARE checklist to report clinical case reports with recommended items for completeness and transparency; apply extensions for specialty areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE (Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines to improve reporting of animal research (ARRIVE 2.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ARRIVE items to ensure methodological and ethical transparency in animal studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE / RIGHT (Guidelines for clinical practice guideline reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: RIGHT statement and AGREE checklist/tools for reporting clinical practice guidelines and assessing guideline reporting quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RIGHT and AGREE items to structure guideline reports and improve transparency about development methods, recommendations, and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: COREQ / SRQR (Qualitative research reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists for reporting qualitative research: COREQ (for interviews and focus groups) and SRQR (Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report study context, researcher reflexivity, sampling, data collection and analysis in line with these checklists; apply topic-specific qualitative reporting guidance when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE (Standards for QUality Improvement Reporting Excellence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication guidelines for quality improvement studies (SQUIRE 2.0 and SQUIRE-SIM/SQUIRE-EDU extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SQUIRE to report improvement interventions, context, measures, and outcomes; extensions cover simulation and educational improvement reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS (Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting standards for economic evaluations and health economic analyses (CHEERS 2022 and related guidance such as CHEERS-VOI and CHEERS-AI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report perspective, methods, model structure, data sources, and uncertainty analyses per CHEERS.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT-AI / SPIRIT-AI / STARD-AI / TRIPOD-LLM and AI-related checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions and new reporting guidelines addressing reporting requirements for studies involving artificial intelligence, machine learning, and large language models in clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These checklists add items on dataset provenance, model development, evaluation, explainability, deployment, and potential biases; apply AI-specific extensions when AI methods are central to the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE / CASE-SPECIFIC extensions (specialty case reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous specialty extensions adapting the CARE or related case-reporting checklists for domains such as acupuncture, radiology, dry needling, physiotherapy, anesthesiology, endodontics, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the case-report checklist extension matching the clinical specialty to ensure domain-specific items are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for animal and preclinical studies (ARRIVE and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and checklists to improve transparency and reproducibility in animal and preclinical research (ARRIVE, REHBaR, and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details on experimental design, randomization, blinding, sample size calculation, humane endpoints and replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of harms and safety (CONSORT Harms and related guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for reporting harms, adverse events, and safety data in clinical trials and other studies (e.g., CONSORT Harms 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report definitions, collection methods, severity grading, denominators, time windows, and attrition relevant to harms reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for specialized trial designs and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions addressing cluster randomised trials, adaptive designs, stepped wedge designs, multi-arm trials, trials using cohorts/routinely collected data, N-of-1 trials, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specific CONSORT (or other primary guideline) extension that matches the trial design to ensure all design-specific reporting items are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines for systematic reviews of specific topics (PRISMA extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRISMA extensions and topic-specific reporting checklists for scoping reviews, network meta-analyses, equity-focused reviews, living reviews, and topic-adapted PRISMA checklists (e.g., for acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the PRISMA variant appropriate to the review question, data types, and methods used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for reporting diagnostic/prognostic modelling and biomarker studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and checklists (e.g., REMARK, STARD, RiGoR, STROBOD, GUIDES for biomarkers) for transparent reporting of prognostic models, biomarker studies, and diagnostic accuracy research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cohort selection, index/test specification, reference standards, statistical modelling, validation, calibration, discrimination, and clinical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for reporting implementation, equity, and public-health oriented studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklists and guidance for implementation research (StaRI), equity-focused reporting (PRISMA-Equity, STROBE-EQUITY), public-health surveillance and outbreak reports (ORION), and reporting of real-world evidence (GROW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include context, implementation processes, adaptations, equity considerations, and data provenance relevant to public-health and implementation sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for reporting methodological and specialty study types
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad set of reporting standards for niche or methodological study types: Delphi studies (DELPISTAR), bibliometric reviews (BIBLIO), concept mapping, consensus methods (ACCORD), simulation studies (STRESS), social media analytics, ecological momentary assessment, and many discipline‑specific checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reporting guideline that matches the methodology or specialty to ensure reporting completeness and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and resources for authors, reviewers, and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary materials such as Authors’ Submission Toolkit, guidance on how to write a guideline, reporting guideline manual, translations, and help pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources explain the Library scope, inclusion criteria, how to search and use reporting guidelines, and provide editorial/author support for applying checklists.
